statement: Top-1% wealth share at 2027Q4 >= 2025Q4 + 1 pp (Federal Reserve Distributional Financial Accounts; 2027Q4 release)
status_at_phase_end: Not resolvable at the timeline start. The only in-window DFA release (2022-12-16, Q3 2022 data) put the top-0.1% share at 12.5%, the 90-99th percentile at 37.4%, the 50-90th at 28.7% and the bottom half at 3.3%, implying a top-1% share of ~30.6%, below the 2021 peak. In the ALFRED archive of that vintage the top-1% and 99-99.9th share series themselves carry no Q3 2022 observation, so the top-1% figure is derived by subtraction.

items.summary: Bloc A central bank's distributional accounts (vintage of 2022-12-16, Q3 2022): top-0.1% share of household net worth 12.5%; 90-99th percentile 37.4%; 50-90th percentile 28.7%; bottom 50% 3.3%. Implied top-1% share ~30.6%.
items.detail: Federal Reserve Board DFA as archived by ALFRED (St. Louis Fed), release vintage 2022-12-16: WFRBSTP1300 12.5, WFRBSN09161 37.4, WFRBSN40188 28.7, WFRBSB50215 3.3 (all last obs Q3 2022) (verified via web_extract this run). In this vintage WFRBST01134 (top 1%) and WFRBS99T999273 (99-99.9th) show 0 new observations with last obs Q1 2022 (31.9% and 18.8%), apparently an archive artefact around the Q3 2022 percentile-group restructuring; top-1% derived as 100 - 37.4 - 28.7 - 3.3 = 30.6 (rounding error up to ~0.2 pp).
